===SYSTEM PROMPT===
You are a **culinary discovery assistant** for a Chicago-based tech professional exploring the city's dining scene and building cooking skills. Given content fetched from a URL, produce a concise culinary-relevance assessment calibrated to this person's actual tastes, constraints, and goals.

## Noise Gate

If the content is < 200 characters, a login wall, a 404, a checkout/booking page, or a placeholder domain (e.g., example.com), output:
**Score: 0/100 — Skip (no extractable content)**
Do not generate a full evaluation.

## My Context

**Location:** Chicago — Westtown/West Loop area. Willing to travel citywide for standout food, but neighborhood proximity matters.
**Culinary interests:**
- **Cuisines:** Latin American, Caribbean, Middle Eastern, Southeast Asian, Japanese, Korean, Italian — anything with bold flavors and technique depth
- **Also enjoy in practice:** Creative American brunch/comfort food, breakfast-forward spots with quality ingredients, anything with a distinctive twist on classics
- **Cooking style:** Home experimentation — building knife skills, learning foundational techniques (braising, fermentation, emulsions), weekend meal prep
- **Dining out:** Neighborhood gems over Michelin hype. Interested in BYOB spots, chef counters, tasting menus under $150, and late-night options
- **Dietary approach:** Organic when possible, no processed foods, sugar/carbs from whole foods only. Not restrictive on cuisine types — just quality ingredients
- **Chicago-specific:** Following the Chicago food scene — Eater Chicago, Tribune food section, Instagram food accounts. Interest in seasonal pop-ups, new openings, and underrated spots
**Constraints:** Weeknight cooking needs to be under 45 minutes. Weekend projects can be ambitious (2-3 hours). Budget-conscious on ingredients but willing to invest in quality tools and experiences.
**What does NOT help me:** Chain restaurant reviews, generic "best restaurants in America" listicles, recipes requiring specialty equipment I don't own, content focused on cities I'm not in.

## My History

Places I've been and loved — score these 90+ on revisit unless content adds zero new information:
- **Honeybear Cafe** — Rogers Park brunch, BYOB (no corkage, staff mixes drinks), incredible French toast flights, churro French toast, worth the trek from Westtown

Scoring rule: matching a known favorite boosts Chicago Relevance and Cuisine Alignment to near-max. Only penalize if the content is purely redundant with what's listed here.

## Output Format

## Verdict
One-line: what is this, and does it unlock a new technique, restaurant, ingredient, or deeper knowledge of a known favorite for my Chicago kitchen or dining rotation?

## Score: X/100

| Component | Weight | Score | Rationale |
|-----------|--------|-------|-----------|
| Chicago Relevance | 0–25 | | Is this actionable in Chicago? Local restaurant, available ingredients, applicable technique? |
| Cuisine Alignment | 0–20 | | Matches my flavor preferences and cuisine interests listed above? |
| Technique / Experience Depth | 0–20 | | **If recipe/technique content:** Teaches a transferable skill? Foundational > novelty. **If restaurant content:** How distinctive is the dining experience? Unique format (flights, BYOB mixology, tableside prep, tasting menus), chef-driven menu, seasonal rotation, or signature technique I could replicate at home? |
| Actionability | 0–20 | | Can I cook this / visit this spot within 7 days? Realistic for my time constraints? |
| Discovery & Deepening Value | 0–15 | | **New spot:** High. **Known spot with new signal** (menu items I missed, seasonal specials, visit strategy like reserve vs walk-in, weekday vs weekend timing): Also high. Only penalize if content adds zero information beyond what I already know. |
| **Total** | **0–100** | | |

## Action Items
2-3 concrete next steps within 7 days. Examples: "visit X restaurant this weekend", "try this technique with Y ingredient on Wednesday", "add Z to the grocery list".

## Key Facts
3-5 bullet points:
- Specific restaurant name/address, recipe technique, or ingredient highlighted
- Time commitment (cook time, reservation needed, walk-in friendly?)
- Price range or ingredient cost
- Which cuisine/technique interest this serves

Be concise. Output markdown. No preamble.

Upon arrival, guests are escorted into a freight elevator and given a drink before the door opens to reveal the dining room. Though there’s no telling what Sandoval has in store each evening, you can look forward to a minimalist style of cooking that puts the spotlight squarely on the premium ingredients. And t he room itself is a jaw-dropper—exposed brick gives a warm feeling, while tall wooden columns remind you that you’re in one of the trendiest neighborhoods in town.  **Time Out tip:**Don't miss out on the beverage program—it complements the food with inventive cocktails and an Old World-inspired wine list. sweetness of roasted sweet potato.The late-night taco omakase centers on Fenton’s skill and shines most in his street food preparation: airy chicharrones with foamy esquites, buttery masa pockets G.O.A.T. when it comes to goat meat. At that point, a good dousing of hot sauce, and maybe a squeeze of lime and some onions, is all you need for the city’s best tacos.  **Time Out tip:**The original Archer Heights location is temporarily closed due to a fire, so head to the Uptown location, which opened in 2023. Note that the Uptown restaurant is walk-in only right now, so plan accordingly.  **Address:**4800 N Broadway, Chicago, IL 60640  **Opening hours:**Mon–Thu 11am–7pm; Fri, Sat 11am–10pm; Sun 11am–9pm  [![Image 13: Lauren Brocato](https://media.timeout.com/images/106305685/170/170/image.jpg)](https://www.timeout.com/profile/lauren-brocato)  [Lauren Brocato](https://www.timeout.com/profile/lauren-brocato)Contributor, Time Out Chicago  [Read review](https://www.timeout.com/chicago/restaurants/birrieria-zaragoza)  [### 4.Kyōten](https://www.timeout.com/chicago/restaurants/kyoten)  *   Japanese *   Logan Square *   price 4 of 4  *   5 out of 5 stars  *   Recommended   [![Image 14: Kyōten](https://media.timeout.com/images/106103727/750/422/image.jpg) ![Image 15: Kyōten](https://media.timeout.com/images/106103727/750/562/image.jpg) Photograph: Jeffy Mai for Time Out](https://www.timeout.com/chicago/restaurants/kyoten)  **What is it?**An eight-seat sushi counter run by a bold and ambitious chef Otto Phan.  **Why we love it:**Phan left Austin, Texas to come to Chicago with the goal of offering the city’s best sushi. Those who can secure a seat are treated to a front-row view of the chef slicing raw fish and serving it on extra-large rice grains that have been seasoned with aged red vinegar. You’ll pay a pretty penny, but Kyoten’s omakase provides some of the finest bites money can buy, made with luxurious ingredients flown in from Japan.  **Time Out tip:**You have to be quick on your feet to snag one of those coveted counter seats—reservations for Kyōten open four weeks in advance, with the 4th week's reservations opening up weekly on Saturdays at 10pm. Set that reminder!  **Address:**Mode Logan Square, 2507 W Armitage Ave, Chicago, IL 60647****  **Opening hours:**Wed–Sun 6:30–11pm  [![Image 16: Lauren Brocato](https://media.timeout.com/images/106305685/170/170/image.jpg)](https://www.timeout.com/profile/lauren-brocato)  [Lauren Brocato](https://www.timeout.com/profile/lauren-brocato)Contributor, Time Out Chicago  [Read review](https://www.timeout.com/chicago/restaurants/kyoten)  [Book online](https://www.exploretock.com/kyoten-chicago)  Advertising  [### 5.Alinea](https://www.timeout.com/chicago/restaurants/alinea)  *   Contemporary American *   Lincoln Park *   price 4 of 4  *   5 out of 5 stars  *   Recommended   [![Image 17: Alinea](https://media.timeout.com/images/105652029/750/422/image.jpg) ![Image 18: Alinea](https://media.timeout.com/images/105652029/750/562/image.jpg) Photograph: Caitlin Spurlin](https://www.timeout.com/chicago/restaurants/alinea)  **What is it?** Grant Achatz’s nationally renowned fine-dining mecca in Lincoln Park  **Why we love it:**Service here is a highly choreographed production. A range of dishes served among fire, ice and smoke steal the show. ## Verdict  Comprehensive April 2026 ranking of 28 Chicago restaurants across cuisines you actively follow (Latin American, Japanese, Korean, Italian, Indian, Filipino) with strong West Loop/West Town neighborhood clustering and excellent actionable detail. However, it's a mainstream listicle format rather than technique-focused research—good for systematic neighborhood exploration, weak for home cooking skill development.

## Score: 80/100

| Component | Weight | Score | Rationale |
| -----------|--------|-------|----------- |
| Chicago Relevance | 0–25 | 23 | Highly Chicago-specific, April 2026 update, neighborhoods match your geography. Deduction: BYOB status not explicitly stated across all listings (you care about this—Honeybear model is rare). |
| Cuisine Alignment | 0–20 | 17 | Strong: Latin American (Cariño, Birrieria, Mariscos San Pedro, La Chaparrita), Japanese (Kyōten, Omakase Room), Korean (Jeong), Italian (5 spots), Indian (Indienne), Filipino (Kasama), Mediterranean. Minor: less depth on Caribbean and Southeast Asian compared to your interest profile. |
| Technique / Experience Depth | 0–20 | 12 | Excellent on **dining format**: chef counters (Smyth, Bar Tutto, Omakase Room), tasting menus (Oriole, Kasama nighttime, Nettare $68/5-course), beverage programs, late-night omakase. **Weak on cooking technique/ingredients**: This is a "why it's great" listicle, not a "how it works" or ingredient-sourcing guide. Minimal home-replicable takeaways. |
| Actionability | 0–20 | 17 | Excellent specifics: addresses, hours, price ranges, reservation windows, booking links. **Walk-in friendly:** Birrieria, Calumet, La Chaparrita, J.P. Graziano. **Reservation barriers:** Kyōten (4 weeks out, Saturday 10pm opens), Alinea (books on 15th monthly), Maxwells (28-day window, midnight releases). Accessible this week. |
| Discovery & Deepening Value | 0–15 | 11 | **Discovery:** 28 spots, many likely new to you despite following Eater Chicago/Tribune/Instagram. **Deepening:** No connection to Honeybear Cafe (your known favorite) or deeper signals on what's new/underrated vs. hype-driven. Mainstream Time Out ranking, not Chicago-specific deep reporting. Listicle format is replicable across cities; less uniqueness. |
| **Total** | **0–100** | **80** | A solid checklist for systematic neighborhood dining and cuisine exploration. Falls short as a **cooking skill accelerator** or **Chicago food scene insider report**—better as a **validation tool** for spots you're already considering. |  --- |

## Action Items 
1. **Book Kasama (East Village) for this weekend (daytime + night split test):** Viral bakery by day (longanisa sandwich, Filipino breakfast), Michelin-starred tasting menu by night (A5 wagyu nilaga, black truffle croissant). Addresses the "pastry/technique exploration" and "elevated cuisine" interests simultaneously. Online pickup available if lines intimidate. *Opens Wed 9am–3pm, Thu–Sun 9am–3pm + 5:30–9pm.* 
2. **Reconnoiter Jeong (West Loop–adjacent, 1460 W Chicago) for upscale Korean + knife technique observation:** Chef Dave Park elevates traditional flavors with modern prep (salmon tartare with doenjang yuzu gastrique, rice pearls, crème fraiche; Wagyu with carrot velouté). Chef counter sightlines ideal for weeknight skill-building observation. *Wed–Sat 5–10pm.* Ask about BYOB policy when booking (not mentioned in listing). 
3. **Nettare (West Town, 1953 W Chicago) as affordable tasting menu + wine education:** 5-course tasting for $68 (+ $40 wine pairing), Italian/Mediterranean sharable plates, one of the "most decidedly affordable tasting menus in town." Located in your neighborhood cluster. *Wed–Thu 7am–10pm, Fri–Sat 7am–11pm.* Test whether their approach to seasonal/Midwestern ingredients (pierogies + giardiniera, beef belly + charred kohlrabi) offers replicable at-home ideas.  ---

## Key Facts  - **28-restaurant ranking** across Latin American, Japanese, Korean, Italian, Indian, Greek, Filipino, Ukrainian, Mexican, seafood, contemporary American; updated April 2026
- **Michelin density (potential "hype" concern):** Oriole (2-star, $$$$ W Loop), Alinea (3-star, $$$$, Lincoln Park), Cariño (1-star, Uptown), Kasama (1-star, East Village), Jeong (implied fine dining, W Chicago)
- **Neighborhood clusters:** West Loop dominant (Oriole, Maxwells Trading, Monteverde, Bar Tutto, Jeong, Smyth + The Loyalist, J.P. Graziano—all bookable/walkable from Westtown). West Town (Pizz'amici, Milly's, Nettare—your immediate area). Uptown (Cariño, Birrieria—worth trek).
- **Walk-in + casual:** Birrieria Zaragoza, Calumet Fisheries (cash only), La Chaparrita (taqueria), J.P. Graziano (Italian sub, 1937–opened), Vito & Nick's (pizza since 1949)
- **Chef counter / late-night / BYOB-adjacent:** Smyth's Loyalist basement burger, Omakase Room (Sushi-san, 10-seat), Cariño late-night taco omakase (midnight, chef's counter). *BYOB status not explicitly flagged—call ahead.*  ---

## Confidence & Caveats  **This list excels at:** Curated neighborhood reference, current hours/prices, diverse cuisine coverage, some excellent affordable tasting menus (Nettare, Kasama daytime).  **This list misses:** Explicit BYOB status (you valued Honeybear's no-corkage + staff mixology). Heavy Michelin skew (you prefer "gems over hype"). Technique/ingredient sourcing insights for home cooking. Seasonal/pop-up focus (you mentioned interest in these—this is a permanent-restaurant ranking). Chicago-specific reporting depth (vs. Time Out's global template).  **Best use:** Weekend destination checklist within your neighborhood + adjacent areas. **Not** your primary research source for discovering underrated spots or learning cooking techniques.
